author: B
request: When I tick a chore it stays there for ages with that Undo button. I'd rather it slid away straight off and the Undo came up somewhere else for a few seconds.
plan: A ticked row stays in its done look for 5 s with an Undo button, then collapses (owner, 2026-10-24, option B). Moving Undo to a transient bar or toast and removing the row at once changes both the timing and what is drawn, and conflicts with the recorded option. Options: keep the row but shorten to 3 s, or a bottom toast with 4 s Undo.
why: Changes timing and the drawn Undo placement, replacing a recorded choice with no decision on the new one.

author: B
request: The Chores tab badge says 3 but I only have two overdue chores on the list.
plan: The badge counts the open items of the viewer's past-due-with-unassigned list. An item completed a moment ago stays in that list for its 5 s Undo grace, so it is counted until the grace ends. Count only items that are not in the recently completed set. The web's badged path counts open items only.
why: Stale count corrected to the documented definition; nothing drawn differently.

author: B
request: On a chore I'd love a Snooze swipe, push it to tomorrow, instead of having to open Edit.
plan: Swipe actions today: Complete leading; Delete outermost and Edit trailing. The swipe-row pattern allows more actions but caps each side at 45% of the row, and the web has no snooze. Options: a third trailing action (buttons shrink), or put Snooze on the leading side beside Complete. No decision on record.
why: Adds a swipe action and affects gestures with no recorded decision.

author: B
request: Groceries rows don't have the little pencil that the chores rows have.
plan: The edit glyph is meant to be square.and.pencil labelled 'Edit {title}' on every to-do page. Groceries builds its rows without the exposed edit action, so the glyph is absent and VoiceOver loses the Edit action too. Pass the same row options as Chores; the todo row is a single component.
why: A new element that the shared row pattern already requires on every page.

author: B
request: When I open Chores after the app has been closed a while it shows old chores for a second and then they all change.
plan: On a cold launch the list shows the cached TodoItems.json from Application Support before the first fetch lands. There is no age limit on that cache. Options: keep showing it however old, show it only if under 6 hours old and otherwise wait for the fetch, or always wait. The screens are identical either way.
why: Only how long a cache may be shown changes; same list, trade-off between instant content and stale content.

author: B
request: After the phone drops signal and comes back the Chores tab badge vanishes for a few seconds.
plan: The badge publisher resets the count to zero when the connection restarts and republishes after the lists refetch. The no-reload-on-reopen rule says a reconnect must not blank a screen. Keep the last published count until a fresh result arrives.
why: Bug against a stated invariant; one correct behaviour, nothing new drawn.

author: B
request: The quick links at the top of Chores are in a different order from the web.
plan: Native lists the first resident, the second resident, Unassigned, Home and Groceries; the web's constants list Groceries first, then the people, then Home. The pages note takes web parity for behaviour and ids, and the order came from the web. Reorder the tiles to match the web; colours and tiles stay.
why: Order of items changes, decided by web parity with one answer.

author: B
request: When I add a chore it always starts as Unassigned. Could it remember who I picked last time?
plan: The add sheet's assignee starts as Unassigned each time. Options: remember the last pick on this device, default to the signed-in viewer, or keep Unassigned. Remembering stores a person's name in UserDefaults; the same Task Name and assignee controls appear either way.
why: Only a starting value of an existing field changes, with a privacy and convenience trade-off.

author: B
request: When I clear every chore it just says 'nothing due. Nice job!'. It would be nice to see how many I finished this week.
plan: The empty state is the copy decided on 2026-10-24 (stray hyphen fixed) with no number. Choreapp can return completed counts, but no mockup or decision exists for extra text. Options: a second line with the weekly count, or a small progress ring above the message.
why: Adds copy or a new element to a screen with no recorded decision.

author: A
request: The Whole Home thermostat shows 72 but the Living Room one says 70 and the house feels 70.
plan: While effectively away the dial is titled Whole Home but reads the eco-away virtual thermostat, and the current temperature was being taken from that entity's attribute instead of the global one; the spec says only the target comes from the dial's entity, with the action line from global. Read current temperature from the entity the dial uses and add a test for the away case.
why: A wrong temperature corrected to what the spec defines.

author: A
request: After I let go of the dial the number jumps back to the old one for a second, then goes to the new one.
plan: The dial holds the committed target through the optimistic overlay, with the Climate page's 2 s revert; the 11 room thermostats can take longer than that to echo a range. Options: keep 2 s, 6 s, or hold until the live value matches with a 10 s ceiling. The ring and readout are identical in each case.
why: Revert window for optimistic state; the same dial.

author: A
request: The orange warning banner about Automatic Thermostat flashes on when I open the app and then goes away.
plan: The warning shows when input_boolean.demo_contact_1 is off; at cold launch the entity is briefly missing and the check treats that as off. The spec says to show it only for an actual off state, and the content-gate notes say entity reads are never gated. Treat a missing entity as no warning until the state arrives.
why: Only when an existing banner shows; the spec gives the answer.

author: A
request: Could the dial also show the outside temperature? I always check the weather separately.
plan: The readout has an action line, the current temperature and a caption (the setpoint, or a range like 68.0 · 75.0), and callers may override lines or hide the caption. The web dial has no outside value. Options: put it in the caption, add a small line under the readout, or show it only on the Whole Home dial.
why: New content in the dial readout; no decision on record.

author: A
request: Changing the mode in the Thermostat Hub pill shuts the menu every time, I want to flip mode then fan without reopening.
plan: The owner chose native pop-up menus on 2026-10-13 over the web's option-tile dialog, and menus close after each pick. Staying open would mean a different control. Options: a segmented row under the pill, one sheet with mode and fan together, or leave the menus and add a recent-choice shortcut.
why: Different control for the same job; earlier decision reopened, options open.

author: A
request: The little vent cards in a room's thermostat look like buttons but nothing happens when I tap them.
plan: Vent cards are read-only per the spec. The action-tiles pattern and the Climate notes say read-only tiles are flat: no chevron, no pressed state, not announced as a button. The vent cards still use the tappable GlassTile style; switch them to the flat variant.
why: Existing action-tiles rule decides the look.

author: A
request: The haptic buzz while dragging the dial is too much, it buzzes on every half degree.
plan: The thermostat-dial pattern calls for selection haptics while dragging, currently one tick per 0.5 degree step. Options: tick per whole degree, tick only at the heat and cool limits, or a softer impact feedback; the HIG says haptics should be subtle and consistent.
why: Changes how the drag feels; no value on record.

author: A
request: App crashes when I open Predictive Comfort and the forecast isn't there yet.
plan: The Current Prediction metrics read attributes off the sensor and force-cast them when the sensor is 'unknown'. The spec says missing values show as unavailable and the Eco pages show 'unavailable until Home Assistant supplies supported options'. Use optional reads in ClimateLogic.predictiveMetrics and add a test for an empty attribute set.
why: A crash fix; one sensible answer.

author: A
request: The Open Contact Sensors card for the Office Window shows a door icon.
plan: The spec says a card gets the window icon when the title names a window, else the door icon (web CONTACT_GROUPS). The native matcher is case-sensitive, so 'Office window' falls through to the door. Make it case-insensitive and cover it with a ClimateLogic test.
why: Icon drawn to the spec's rule.

author: C
request: That little spinner next to Quick Links flashes up every time I unlock my phone, then goes. Kind of distracting.
plan: The reconnecting arc shows only once the connection has been down 2 s, and after an unlock the foreground reconnect often needs about 2.5 s, so it flashes. The arc, its 0.35 s fade and the no-text rule stay fixed. Options: raise the delay to about 4 s, hold it back for a few seconds after foreground, or leave it.
why: Only the threshold deciding when an existing arc appears; same look and motion.

author: C
request: The offline chip pops up the second I step into the lift or a tunnel and is gone a moment later.
plan: With no network path the app shows the offline chip and the Profile badge at once, and a path blip of one or two seconds is common on cellular hand-off. Chip and badge stay as designed. Options: wait about 3 s without a path before showing them, or keep showing at once.
why: A threshold for when an existing chip shows, no change to the chip.

author: C
request: If I leave the app for a minute and come back there's a catch-up moment. Can it stay connected longer?
plan: The connection stays up for a 30 s grace after backgrounding (`ConnectionLifecycle.backgroundGrace`), then disconnects; on return views update in place from about 40 changed entities. Options: 2 minutes, stay until iOS suspends, or keep 30 s. A longer hold costs battery and iOS may reclaim the socket anyway. Nothing drawn changes.
why: How long the app stays connected: a battery against freshness trade-off with the same screens.

author: C
request: If I open the app after a week away it flashes last week's values for a second. Should it still do that?
plan: `EntitySnapshotCache` loads whatever was saved at any age and a cold launch draws it at once (no intro, 0.2 s cross-fade). There is no age limit. Options: keep it indefinitely, drop snapshots older than a day (launch then looks like a first sign-in with pending bars, which already exists), or a week. Trade-off between old house state on disk and a fast first frame.
why: How long a cached snapshot is kept and trusted; privacy against launch speed, with only existing states shown.

author: C
request: My partner used my phone once and the 'Welcome back, Sam' screen made it awkward. There needs to be a way to sign in as somebody else.
plan: After a rejected token `AppSession.sessionExpired` keeps the last username and first name and shows Welcome back with a monogram and only a password field; there is no way to change the account. Auth forbids storing the password. Options: a 'Not Sam?' link that clears `RememberedAccount` and shows the full form, or a small menu on the monogram. No decision on record.
why: Adds a control to the sign-in screen; two shapes, nothing recorded.

author: C
request: Typed my password wrong and the box keeps the dots, I have to wipe them by hand.
plan: The sign-in spec says that after a wrong password the red line shows, the password row gets a red hairline, the field clears and takes focus, the username stays, and VoiceOver announces it. The clear and the focus are applied only on the first failure in `LoginModel`; the second leaves the old text. Apply the documented sequence every time.
why: Brings the sign-in screen back to behaviour its spec already states.

author: C
request: After I've been away the cameras on Home are black frames that say Live until I leave the page.
plan: Matches the camera-streams notes: a restart from `willEnterForeground` asks for a signed path on a socket about to be replaced and waits forever, and a stopped model kept its live phase. The rule is that nothing asking Home Assistant starts on foreground without `ensureLive`, a timeout, or a restart on `didBecomeReadyNotification`. Check the starter follows it.
why: A logic bug leaving a wrong state, fixed by an existing rule; no new look.

author: C
request: Every time I launch I get 'Connecting to Home Assistant' up top even though all my values are already there.
plan: By the loading-states record the shared 'Connecting to Home Assistant' arc is for a first sign-in only (`hasReceivedFirstState` false, freshness empty); a snapshot launch counts as heard-from and waits out the usual 2 s like a reconnect. A recent change derives `isFirstConnect` from the socket status instead of freshness; derive it from freshness again.
why: A wrong state corrected to what the loading-states record already specifies.

author: C
request: My phone gets warm and the battery drops fast when the app is just sitting open on the desk on wifi.
plan: Reconnect churn: the router rules say a network change forgets home and a public socket stays, but the path filter now lets tunnel and cellular-beside-Wi-Fi updates through, so a phone lying still reconnects one to three times per 8 s (about 50 ms of main thread each). Check `net_changes` and the route counters from `ios_scrollcost.sh` and restore the path signature check.
why: Battery and CPU only, covered by the documented router and path-filter rules.

author: C
request: When I'm offline I only get a chip. I'd like it to say how old the numbers are, but only once it's been a while.
plan: Offline shows the chip and Profile badge over snapshot values (`freshness` is `.snapshot(savedAt)`), and nothing says how old they are. Adding something like 'Updated 12 min ago' is new copy, and it needs a threshold for when it appears (say after 5 minutes). No record of the wording, its place (in the chip or under the header) or the threshold.
why: New words on the offline state and a timing for when they appear, with no decision on record.

author: C
request: When Home Assistant restarts it takes ages for the app to come back by itself.
plan: After a socket failure HAKit's own backoff applies; the router forces an immediate public reconnect only when a home-address socket drops. Options: a capped faster retry (2, 4, 8 s up to 30 s), which spends radio and loads Home Assistant while it boots, or keep HAKit's. The arc and the values behave the same.
why: Retry and backoff timing for an existing reconnect; a battery and server-load trade-off.

author: A
request: Dragging a pathlight light's brightness is laggy, the light follows a second behind my finger.
plan: Brightness tiles send on release, and the system color picker sends 250 ms after it settles; there is no streaming while dragging. The web sends continuously. Options: stream every 100 ms while dragging (smoother, but floods the Zigbee mesh with eight lights), 300 ms, or keep release-only.
why: Send frequency while dragging; cost to the mesh versus responsiveness.

author: A
request: When I pick a color the light changes about a second after I let go of the wheel.
plan: Color picks go out 250 ms after the picker settles so a drag does not flood the light, and the light itself fades in with the transition value. Option: keep 250 ms, shorten to 100 ms (more calls on a spin), or send the final color on dismiss. Nothing in the sheet looks different.
why: Debounce delay on an existing control.

author: A
request: Reset All Lights wiped my custom colors when I fat-fingered it. It should check first.
plan: Reset All Lights is its own card and sends light.turn_on to light.demo_front_yard_1 at 2000 K, 255 brightness at once, as the web does. The security alert and the rooms pages ask before destructive actions, but nothing is recorded for this one. Options: a confirmation alert, an undo toast, or keep it single-tap and move it further from the tiles.
why: Adds a confirmation or undo; no decision on record.

author: A
request: The Team Colors swatch in Lighting Mode is the wrong way round, it should go green to blue.
plan: The spec lists Team Colors as rgb(0,255,0) to rgb(0,0,255) and Holiday Mode as rgb(255,0,0) to rgb(255,0,234). The native swatch gradient is drawn from the blue end first because the stops are reversed in CustomLightsConfig. Restore the documented stops and update the existing config test.
why: Colour redrawn to the documented spec.

author: A
request: Left Door Light says 100% when it's turned off.
plan: The tile reads the brightness attribute, which Home Assistant keeps at the last value while the light is off. The entity-tile pattern says an off light shows Off and the sheet subtitle shows 'Off', as the web LightBrightnessCard does. Gate the displayed brightness on the state being on.
why: A wrong value corrected to what the design shows (state off).

author: A
request: Reset to Warm White is too orange, can it be a bit whiter?
plan: The web resets to color_temp_kelvin 2000 with brightness 255, and the native app copies it for Reset All Lights and the per-light Reset. Options: keep 2000 K, 2200 K or 2700 K (typical warm white); the lights change but nothing in the app does, and the web would stay at 2000 unless changed too.
why: Value of an existing reset default; the owner has to choose.

author: A
request: In the light sheet, the Copy Color From circles are hard to tell apart, can they show what color it is by name?
plan: The grid shows a colour circle with the light's name under it, and 'Off' for an off light. The spec and web only copy the rgb_color without naming it. Options: a hex or colour name under each circle, a tiny 'warm/cool' hint, or a long-press preview; the name would need localisation.
why: Adds text to a control; no decision on record.

author: A
request: VoiceOver reads the brightness tile as 'Left Door Light, 0.78'.
plan: The tile's accessibility value uses the raw slider fraction. The entity-tile pattern says light tiles read a percentage and the sheet subtitle already says '78%'. Make the VoiceOver value the shared percent string and keep the Turn On/Off action; add the accessibility test.
why: Spoken value fixed to the existing pattern.

author: C
request: CI takes forever on the mini, the queue is always full.
plan: Simulators and heavy compiles run in `devcap` holds, with machine-wide slots shared with FestivalNativeApps, on an 8 GB mini. Full coverage and the three-device runs already happen once per PR. Options: fewer slots per run with the lean simulator profile for filtered runs, run only affected tiers from the test plans, or longer queue times. The app does not change.
why: A cost, time and coverage trade-off in tooling with nothing on screen.

author: C
request: ResumeCyclesJourneyTests keeps failing on the Duo sim and passing on rerun.
plan: The census is read right after the first scroll, before the 30 s grace timer finishes on a slow slot. Wait on the `diagnostics.resources` value with a bounded deadline instead of a fixed delay, as the weather briefing test did in #266.
why: Test stability only.

author: C
request: I think release builds log telemetry even though the Performance switch says off.
plan: Telemetry should record only in Debug builds, with `FENTON_TELEMETRY=1`, or with the Performance switch on, and nothing leaves the device unless exported (telemetry pattern). `PerfSwitches` reads a missing key as true. Default it to false.
why: A default value corrected to what the telemetry pattern already states.

author: C
request: Recipes feels laggy to scroll whenever the house is busy, like when the dishwasher and lights are updating.
plan: The invariant is that a live change costs the main thread one box update and the diff runs on `deltaQueue`. A recipe tile reading a whole-store observable would re-render on every delivery. Measure with `tools/ios_scrollcost.sh` (`upd ms`, `>8ms`) and bind to per-entity boxes. No layout change.
why: Scroll smoothness and CPU; the rule and the measuring tool are already recorded.

author: C
request: I'd like to know how the app is doing on a family member's phone without her exporting a file by hand.
plan: Telemetry stays on device and the Performance screen's Export Telemetry shares one JSON file; MetricKit payloads are kept under Caches. Options: opt-in upload to Home Assistant on the relay path, send only MetricKit hitch summaries, or keep manual export. Records carry page names and entity ids but never values; the screens do not change.
why: What data leaves the device and how often; a privacy and effort trade-off with the same screens.

author: C
request: The sims keep getting left booted and the other project can't get a slot.
plan: AGENTS says never boot a simulator outside a `devcap` hold. The ad hoc script boots with `simctl` before taking its hold and leaves it up on failure. Wrap the boot in `devcap run --sim` and shut it down on exit.
why: Tooling fix to a documented rule.

author: C
request: The Performance screen is a wall of numbers. Give me a summary at the top so I can see in a second whether something's bad.
plan: Settings -> Performance lists scrolling per page, navigation per surface, page loading, live updates, actions and images, with Export Telemetry. Budgets exist in performance.md (8 ms turns at 120 Hz). There is no summary and no record of how to show one. Options: a status row per section with a good or over-budget mark, or a single headline number.
why: New element on a screen with no recorded design.

author: C
request: On the Performance screen the Export Telemetry button label is cut off at large text and the share sheet doesn't come up.
plan: The button should follow the settings-section rules for rows (wraps, 44 pt, AX5 audit) and open the share sheet with the JSON file. The label is one line and the share is requested before the file is written. Let the label wrap and write the file first.
why: Visible fix with one answer from existing patterns and HIG.

author: C
request: The Performance screen shows 0 ms worst turn for Settings even though I just scrolled it a lot.
plan: Settings moved to `InsetGroupedStack`, a `ScrollView`, and the new scroll view lacks `.scrollTelemetry("Settings")`, so it records no samples and the screen prints 0. The pattern says every page's main scroll view carries the modifier. Add it; the screen itself is unchanged.
why: A wrong number corrected so the screen shows what it was designed to show.

author: C
request: Do quick journey runs have to use all three devices? It's slow when I'm only checking a small fix.
plan: The owner's device rule (2026-10-10) says every automation and accessibility test runs on iPhone, iPhone Duo and iPad, and the full three-device run happens once per PR. How a quick filtered run during development should behave is not written down. Options: iPhone only until the PR check, or touched-family only via the test map. This is tooling only.
why: How much testing runs while developing, a speed against risk trade-off with no change to the app.

author: C
request: When the triage agent opens a PR for something I filed, ping me in the app.
plan: A push path exists (Fenton Push, taps open sections or a link), and the triage agent files through the Home Assistant relay, but nothing notifies the reporter. A new notification needs wording, a tap target (the PR on GitHub or Settings -> Feedback), and whether it is Time Sensitive. No decision on record.
why: New notification copy and tap behaviour with no recorded choice.

author: B
request: Tapping All Recipes shows a spinner for what feels like forever. Could the grid just appear with grey placeholder cards while it loads?
plan: The page sits in a content gate with the web's timings: 1 s minimum spinner, 500 ms exit, 170 ms enter (owner, 2026-10-16: spinner, fade out, content fade in). Placeholder cards would replace the spinner and change both what shows and when. Options: skeleton grid with no minimum wait, or keep the spinner and drop the minimum to 0.5 s.
why: Changes timing and what is drawn while loading, replacing a recorded loading behaviour.

author: B
request: Recipe photos blink when I come back to the recipes grid, like they're loading all over again.
plan: Recipe image URLs carry a rotating sig parameter that the image cache does not strip, so the key changes whenever Home Assistant re-signs the URL and the cache misses. The image-cache pattern says the key ignores rotating tokens; add sig to that list. A same-key refresh swaps without animation already.
why: Cache-key bug against the image-cache pattern; no look change beyond removing the blink.

author: B
request: A recipe says 8/9 ingredients but I have all of them, every row says I have it.
plan: The subtitle count uses the response's available flag, while the ingredient rows decide from the inventory match and treat optional items as covered. The count undercounts by the optional ingredient. Compute the count from the same per-row result; the rows themselves already read correctly.
why: Wrong number corrected to what the rows already show.

author: B
request: I want to sort recipes by cook time.
plan: The sort sheet offers Ingredients Available and Name, matching the web; the summary line under the title says 'Sorted by Ingredients Available'. Cook time is in the recipe data but no sort or filter uses it. Options: a Cook Time option in the same sheet, or a quick-filter chip. No decision on record.
why: Adds a sort option and changes the summary line with no recorded decision.

author: B
request: The suggested recipes on the Food page are different every time I come back to it.
plan: The hub requests suggestions each time it appears and each call asks the recipe service to rank the inventory. Options: keep the same set for the session, refresh after 30 minutes, or every visit as today. Less frequent means fewer service calls and a steadier hub; the carousel and cards are unchanged.
why: Only how often suggestions refresh changes; same carousel, trade-off between freshness and calls.

author: B
request: After I add a recipe to the grocery list it just says 'Added to Grocery List'. I want to know how many things it added.
plan: The done state reads 'Added to Grocery List' (owner, 2026-10-16) and the button sits under an explanation line. The service response includes the added items, so the count is available. Options: 'Added 3 Items to Grocery List', or the names listed beneath the button.
why: Changes on-screen copy beyond a recorded string, with no decision on the new wording.

author: B
request: At the biggest text size the Instructions tab of a Cookidoo recipe gets cut off at the top and I can't scroll up to step 1.
plan: The Instructions tab centres its content with a minimum height equal to the sheet. At AX5 the steps are taller than the sheet but the centring still offsets them. The recorded rule (owner, 2026-10-16) is: steps that fit are centred, longer ones scroll from the top. Apply the same basedOnSize bounce and top alignment rule when content exceeds the height.
why: Layout fixed back to a recorded owner decision; one answer.

author: B
request: The recipe cards on iPhone are too small to read the titles. Can they be bigger?
plan: RecipeGrid uses a 160 pt minimum column (2 to 8 columns), with image cards. On an iPhone that gives two columns with titles over two lines. Options: raise the minimum so titles get more room, a single wide card column with a larger photo, or let the owner toggle grid and list. No decision on record.
why: Changes layout and sizes with no recorded density decision; several options.

author: B
request: I used up my last egg but the recipe I can now not make is still at the top of the list.
plan: Sorted by Ingredients Available uses availability counts fetched with the page and not refreshed when inventory entities change, so the order stays stale until a manual reload. Recompute availability on the next page fetch and on inventory-change events; the sort rule itself is unchanged.
why: Stale ordering data corrected; the sort and screen stay as documented.

author: A
request: Sometimes when I open the app the status chips at the top say Unavailable for a split second and then fill in with the real numbers.
plan: On a cold launch the chips read the live store before the disk snapshot is merged, so for one frame the Lights and Contact Sensors entities count as missing. The Home spec already says a snapshot renders its saved values at once and only a genuinely missing or unavailable entity shows 'Unavailable'. The fix is to read the restored snapshot first so the chips never pass through the missing state.
why: Only when an existing 'Unavailable' state appears changes; the spec already fixes the one correct behaviour.

author: A
request: The weather card is showing yesterday's numbers when I open the app in the morning, it takes a few minutes to catch up.
plan: The forecast store restores its disk copy on launch but never treats it as fresh, then refetches; the cache lifetime is 5 minutes like the web. Refresh on open is therefore already immediate, so the lag comes from the TTL after a successful fetch. Options: keep 5 minutes, drop to 2 (more calls to the weather integration, more battery), or go to 15 (fewer calls, staler numbers). No decision on record.
why: Cache lifetime trade-off between freshness and data/battery with the same card.

author: A
request: The high on the weather card says 61 but when I open the weather sheet it says 64.
plan: The card derives today's high from the hourly list cached at launch while the sheet reads the daily forecast entry after refetching, so after a day boundary they disagree. The weather pattern says both use the same daily entry, as the web WeatherSummary does. Point the card at the shared daily entry; no layout changes.
why: A wrong value corrected to what the design already shows.

author: A
request: When I turn on the guest room toggle the guest section just appears and shoves the cameras down, it's jarring.
plan: The guest presence section is inserted as soon as one of the three guest booleans is on, with no transition. The motion pattern covers tile state changes but has nothing for sections that appear or disappear, and the web just conditionally renders. Options: fade and slide the section in, expand it from a header row, or leave it as is and animate only the cameras below.
why: Adds motion to a section appearing; no decision on record for how.

author: A
request: Cameras take forever to come back when I go Home, Climate, then Home again, but they're instant if I only go to Security and back.
plan: The camera pool pauses a stream 4 s after no view shows it, to stop WebRTC decode burning CPU behind pages without cameras (measured 2.8 to 3.2 s versus 0.85 s). Climate has no camera, so the stream is paused and must restart. Options: keep 4 s, extend to 30 or 60 s, or never pause while the app is foregrounded; each trades battery and heat for faster return. Nothing on record about the preferred value.
why: How long a stream stays connected: battery versus speed, same screens.

author: A
request: I want a Cameras shortcut in Quick Links so I can jump to the camera section without scrolling Home.
plan: Quick Links today lists Rooms, Security System, Food & Recipes, Vacuums, Media, Custom Lights and Sprinklers; the web action has no cameras entry and cameras live only as a section on Home and Security. A new entry would need a destination (scroll to the section, the Security tab, or a dedicated camera grid) and an icon and position. No decision on record.
why: New Quick Links entry and what a tap opens; no decision on record.

author: A
request: The Contact Sensors chip says '1 Open' but every door and window is shut.
plan: The chip counted a sensor whose state is unavailable as open. The spec defines the chip as 'All Closed' or 'N Open' across the contact sensors, and unavailable sensors are shown dimmed in the overview, not counted. Count only sensors in state on; the Security tab chip shares the same helper.
why: A count corrected to the documented definition.

author: A
request: The Air Quality chip shows 'AQI 42 · PM2.5 8.000000001', way too many digits.
plan: The chip prints the raw input_text value for the PM2.5 range. The web formats it through formatCompactEntityState to one decimal with a trailing .0 dropped, and the entity-tile pattern states the same rule for numbers. Apply that formatter in the chip summary and VoiceOver value.
why: Number format is drawn text but follows an existing pattern and web parity.

author: A
request: The weather summary at 6am still talks about last night's rain instead of what the day looks like.
plan: The day briefing is generated once per local day at or after 00:01 and stored in the disk snapshot, so it describes the forecast as of just after midnight. Options: keep 00:01, freeze at 05:00 so it reflects the morning forecast, or regenerate when the first forecast of the day arrives. Same card and same copy templates in all cases; later generation costs one extra forecast fetch.
why: When the briefing is generated: timing trade-off with the same card and copy.

author: A
request: The 'reconnecting' arc takes too long to show up, and honestly a little spinner is easy to miss, I'd like it to say Reconnecting in words and appear in about a second.
plan: The arc shows after 2 s without a connection per the Home spec; there is no text. The status-pill and state-message patterns offer a labelled inline message, and the web has no reconnect indicator at all. Options: shorter delay with the same arc, a header caption 'Reconnecting…', or a slim banner under the title; the delay and the copy would change together.
why: Changes both the delay and the drawn indicator with copy; no decision on record.

author: B
request: Scan Item takes a while to say it found the barcode, I have to hold the item still for ages.
plan: The scanner needs three identical reads in a row before it accepts a code, to avoid wrong adds. Two reads would be about 400 ms quicker with more risk of a misread being accepted. Options: keep three, two, or two plus a checksum validation. The camera card and 'Looking for a Barcode' pill do not change.
why: Only a confirmation threshold changes; same camera, same pill, accuracy against speed.

author: B
request: After I add prepared food the list shows an extra row for a moment and then it jumps back.
plan: Prepared food shows the expected batches at once, then re-reads the inventory every 1 s until it matches or 10 s pass (web PREPARED_REFRESH_RETRY_MS). The extra row is the expectation before the real batch arrives. Options: keep 1 s, re-read every 2 s with a 15 s cap (less traffic, slower settle), or settle after the first match.
why: Only retry cadence and cap change; the same expected row and list appear.

author: B
request: Something that expires in 8 days is orange under Expiring Soon, but the page says soon means within a week.
plan: The row tone and the Expiring Soon group both judge on the local calendar, but the count in the 'N Expiring Soon' line still uses Pantryhub's UTC days_remaining and is off by one near midnight. Use InventoryCalendar for the line and the row tint; the sections already do.
why: A wrong value corrected to the documented local-calendar judgement.

author: B
request: Can Expiring Soon be two weeks instead of one?
plan: Soon is within 7 days (the same judgement for the orange text, the Expiring Soon section and the 'N Expiring Soon' count; web uses 7). Widening only moves items into the same orange state earlier. Options: 14 days for everyone, 10 days, or a setting in the filter sheet; no new screens for the first two.
why: blind: one option adds a filter-sheet setting; any drawn option makes it design

author: B
request: The inventory list would feel better with a small photo of each product.
plan: Item rows carry no thumbnail: InventoryItem does not parse image_url and the web rows have none (design pass 2026-10-16 left it out). Adding it needs the image field, the image cache and a row layout change. Options: 44 pt leading thumbnail, or photos only in the editor header.
why: Adds an element and changes the row layout; no decision on record for adding images.

author: B
request: I changed a quantity in the item editor and saved, but the list behind it still shows the old number until I leave and come back.
plan: saveChanges() writes every changed batch and closes, but only refreshLoaded() on the editor's own model; the page's InventoryListModel is not told. Call the list's refresh after the batches finish, as the add flow does. The spec says Home Assistant owns every change, then the page re-reads.
why: Stale value on a screen corrected to the documented re-read.

author: B
request: On Scan Item there's no way to turn on the flashlight so I can't scan in the pantry.
plan: The 4:5 camera card has a status pill and nothing else on it; no torch control exists and the web has none. Options: a circular torch toggle in the card's corner, or a toggle in the manual-entry footer. No decision on record.
why: Adds a new control to a screen with no recorded decision.

author: B
request: The empty pantry shows Scan Item as a little round button, but I thought it had a label on an empty page.
plan: The inventory pattern says Scan Item is a titled glass capsule on an empty page and a bare glyph otherwise. On iPad the empty-state check uses the filtered count rather than the loaded count, so the capsule never shows there. Use the loaded count; the capsule already exists.
why: Control shown with a label, decided by the recorded empty-page rule.

author: B
request: Typing in inventory search stutters on my iPhone once there are a lot of items.
plan: Each keystroke regroups all items by lowercased name and re-sorts on the main thread. Cache the grouped catalogue, filter off the main actor and publish once per typing pause. Measure with the scroll-cost tool before and after; results and layout are identical.
why: Pure performance work; same results on screen.

author: B
request: Make the inventory sort by expiration date to begin with, not by title.
plan: Sort starts at Title, which gives one headerless list; Expiration Date gives Expired, Expiring Soon, Later and No Expiration Date groups. Both options exist already. Options: default to expiry everywhere, default only for fridge and freezer spaces, or remember the last pick per space.
why: rubric clarification 2026-11-02: a default that regroups the page is drawn differently

author: B
request: The volume slider on the Living Room Streamer tile jumps back to the old level for a second after I let go, then goes to the right number.
plan: The tile slider writes on release and the controller holds its own value for 2.5 s. The Streamer reports the new volume about 3 s later, so the hold ends before the echo and the old level shows in between. Options: hold up to 5 s, or hold until the echo with an 8 s cap; the cost is a stale value for longer if the call silently fails. No decision on record for the hold length.
why: Only the length of an existing hold changes; same slider, same look, trade-off between staleness and snap-back.

author: B
request: I switch the Studio to Game Console and the tile flips back to Off for a moment before it settles on On.
plan: The optimistic Game Console value is cleared by any live change, including unrelated entities, so the tile drops to the stale sensor value. The web's held-device state only clears on the source's own reset entities, and the media-remote pattern says to match it. Fix the clear rule to the reset-entity list; the 45 s hold stays as is.
why: Wrong intermediate state corrected to the documented web behaviour; no drawn change and one answer.

author: B
request: The Apps tab in the remote is a lot of scrolling. Could the app tiles be smaller so I can see more of them at once?
plan: App tiles are artwork squares with the name under them in a grid sized by the sheet width, with a pink ring and 'Playing' while active. The pattern records the square tiles but nothing on how many per row. Options: more, smaller columns on iPhone, or a compact list row like the Devices section; both change what is drawn.
why: Changes layout and sizes with no recorded decision on tile density; owner must choose between options.

author: B
request: Game on the Media page still shows a generic controller icon instead of the real logo.
plan: The artwork lives in the web app's bundle, not on the server; the tile falls back to its icon until /local/images/apps/Game.jpg exists. The media-remote pattern already says the tile picks the image up once the file is on the server, so the app needs no change, only the file copied into Home Assistant's www folder.
why: author: the tile draws the logo once the file exists; the pattern decides it

author: B
request: Opening the Living Room remote sits on a spinner for ages on bad wifi, and then everything pops in at once. I'd rather see the remote straight away and have the app icons fill in as they arrive.
plan: The remote is a content gate that waits for every app tile's artwork, up to 4 s, then fades the whole sheet in (owner, 2026-10-13: spinner, then one fade). Showing the sheet immediately with placeholder squares that fill in reverses that recorded choice. Options: keep the gate but give up after 2 s, or open at once with placeholders.
why: Moves timing and changes what is drawn while loading, reversing a recorded loading behaviour with no decision on the replacement.

author: B
request: If I tap the Streamer d-pad quickly on the iPad in landscape, every second press doesn't do anything.
plan: In two-column layout the d-pad buttons share a duplicate-tap guard meant for the keyboard Send button, so a press inside the guard window is swallowed. Streamer presses go straight to remote.send_command (owner, 2026-10-15), so every press should be sent. Remove the guard from the d-pad path and add a test for rapid presses.
why: Crash-free logic bug; one correct behaviour already recorded, nothing drawn differently.

author: B
request: The Studio remote says the volume is 40 but the receiver display says 45.
plan: The volume card shows volume_level times 100 truncated, while the web rounds to the nearest integer, and the entity reports 0.449. Use the same rounding as the web in the shared formatter. The slider position and the service call values stay unchanged.
why: A wrong value corrected to what the web shows; no new design.

author: B
request: Can the playing tiles on the Media page get a mute button next to the volume slider?
plan: Tiles for a playing, paused or buffering remote show previous, play/pause and next discs under the text plus a volume slider; Mute exists only inside the remote's volume card. No decision on record for a tile mute. Options: a fourth disc in the row, or a speaker glyph at the slider's leading end that toggles mute.
why: Adds a new control to a tile with no recorded decision; two options to choose between.

author: B
request: On the Media page the Power button next to an off TV is grey, but in the remote it's green and goes red when on. They should look the same.
plan: The media-remote pattern fixes the power colour rule: red while on, green while every rule entity is inactive, shared by the remote and the page's lead tiles. The tile's Power disc skips the rule and uses the neutral face. Point it at the same power-colour helper; no new colours.
why: Colour change decided by an existing pattern rule applied consistently.

author: C
request: I'd like to see which jobs are running on my wrist and stop the dishwasher from there.
plan: The Watch app is a target stub. The Live Activity model (jobs, phases, focus, controls via `JobControlIntent`) already mirrors to Apple Watch through the Smart Stack, but nothing is specified for an app. Options: a glance list of running jobs with a stop button on each, or only complications and rely on the Smart Stack. Nothing is recorded for its screens.
why: A new Watch surface with no spec or recorded choice.

author: C
request: A home-screen widget would be handy: who's home and whether the front door is locked.
plan: `FentonHomeWidgets` holds only the Live Activity; there is no home-screen or lock-screen WidgetKit widget and no spec. Options: a small widget with person chips and the lock state, or lock-screen accessories only. Colour would follow the saved app icon choice read from the app group, as the activity does.
why: A new widget with no decision on its content or size.

author: C
request: Searching 'dishwasher' in Spotlight should take me to the dishwasher. Is that doable?
plan: Nothing in the app indexes into Spotlight today. Entities, rooms and pages could be donated (CSSearchableItem) and a result opens through the same section links as notifications. Which items count, what the result shows (icon, subtitle) and whether it needs an App Intent is undecided.
why: A new surface (search results and what a tap opens) with no recorded choice.

author: C
request: The lock screen activity sometimes says 'Updating...' after a few minutes even though the job's still going.
plan: The stale date is the earliest end plus 10 minutes; a list with no end times gets now plus 30 minutes, and the engine re-pushes the same state every 25 minutes at priority 5. A stale view shows 'Updating...'. Options: re-push every 15 minutes (more of Apple's roughly three-an-hour budget), lengthen the stale date, or leave it. The text and view are the same in all.
why: Frequency of an existing re-push and when the existing 'Updating...' state shows; battery and push budget trade-off.

author: C
request: The dishwasher 'Done' sits on my lock screen way longer than it should. Or maybe not long enough, I never see it.
plan: A finished job shows 'Done' with a checkmark for the linger time, then the activity ends. The view is the same either way. Options: 2 minutes, 10 minutes, or until the next phone unlock; longer lingers use the activity slot and the island, shorter ones are missed.
why: Only how long an existing 'Done' state stays.

author: C
request: I tapped the chores notification on the lock screen and the app opened Home instead of the chore list.
plan: Links are read the way the web reads them (`routes.ts` `routePathFromUrl`): chores and its sub-routes open the Chores section. A push for `chores/upcoming/` has a trailing slash that isn't trimmed, so it falls back to Home. Trim as the web does.
why: What a tap opens, fixed to web parity.

author: C
request: The doorbell notification shows the picture but the buttons I set in the automation are gone.
plan: Camera notifications get the fixed `fenton.camera` category and the content extension sets the buttons from the payload at runtime. The service extension drops `actions` when the attachment download fails. The push spec says anything that fails leaves the notification as sent, so keep the actions.
why: Buttons restored to the documented behaviour; one answer.

author: C
request: Make 'Show count on app icon' off for new installs. A family member hates the number.
plan: `showAppIconBadge` is an existing Appearance switch, default on (badge.md). Only its starting value changes to off; the control, the number and the badge sent by Fenton Push (`aps.badge`) are unchanged. The owner has already said which value.
why: A default value of an existing setting, chosen by the owner in the request.

author: C
request: Should Time Sensitive be on from the start? I never remember to turn it on and I've missed the garage alerts.
plan: The Setup flow's Time Sensitive step starts off. Options: pre-select it with the notification permission, leave it off and prompt after the first alert that would have qualified, or keep it. Same switch and copy; trade-off is breaking through Focus against missed alarms.
why: A default of an existing setting with an interruption against missed alert trade-off.

author: C
request: I tapped Stop on the dishwasher on the lock screen with no signal and the app crashed.
plan: `JobControlIntent` sets the job to `stopping`, hides its controls, posts `fenton_live_activity_action` with a 10 s timeout and restores the controls on failure. The restore path looks the job up by index after a push may already have ended it. Look it up by tag and do nothing if it's gone.
why: A crash fix with no change to what is shown.

author: C
request: With three jobs running the lock screen activity cuts off the dishwasher's name.
plan: Per live-activities-per-job (decision 5) several jobs show two compact rows, title and status on one line, the focus outlined, inside the 160 pt limit. The status column is a fixed width and squeezes titles. Use the specified row metrics so the title truncates last.
why: Visible layout fix to a recorded spec; one answer.

author: A
request: On the folded Duo the Security System row in Quick Links is squeezed and the text is cut off.
plan: The Rooms spec records the owner's 2026-11-01 decision: Security System takes a full row where two tracks cannot hold its text, and the folded Duo's sheet is then five rows and scrolls (action-tiles pattern). The row is currently still sized as one track. Apply the recorded layout and add the folded-Duo UX test.
why: Layout fixed back to a recorded owner decision.

author: A
request: The room grid in Quick Links keeps shuffling the rooms around right after I open one.
plan: Rooms are ranked by a per-room access counter, and opening a room calls script.demo_script_2, which bumps the counter and re-sorts the open grid immediately. The web ranks on the same counters. Options: re-rank live, only when the sheet is next opened, or once per day; none of them changes the grid itself.
why: When an existing ordering is recomputed; no new screen.

author: A
request: The bathroom fan tile flips back to Off for a moment after I turn it on, then goes On again.
plan: The fan script takes about 3 s to echo, but the optimistic value reverts after 2 s (web useOptimisticState). Longer holds the tapped value longer if the fan never turns on. Options: keep 2 s, 5 s, or wait for the live change with a 10 s ceiling like the humidifier's 8 s.
why: Revert timing of optimistic state; same tile.

author: A
request: The humidifier sheet should show the target humidity as a big number like the thermostat does, I can't read it from across the room.
plan: HumidifierSheet today lists the target as a stepper row in a DeviceSection. The room-device-sheets pattern defines tiles, segmented rows and one main action, and the thermostat-dial pattern is for climate entities only; the web modal shows a plain number. Options: a large numeral header above the controls, a dial for humidity, or bigger stepper text.
why: New presentation of a value in a sheet; no decision on record.

author: A
request: The dishwasher tile just lists a bunch of entities when I tap it, it should be a proper sheet like the fan.
plan: The Rooms notes say the dishwasher is the open hook point: RoomDeviceModal.resolve falls back to a read-only list until its lane lands, and the web has no dedicated dishwasher modal. The room-device-sheets pattern gives chrome and tile rules but not which controls a dishwasher needs (start, delay, cycle, status). No decision on record.
why: A new sheet whose content is undecided.

author: A
request: The Primary Bedroom card says 72.00°F but the sheet says 72.
plan: Room card subtitles join entity values with ' • ' and units; the card prints the raw string while the sheet formats. The entity-tile and thermostat-dial patterns say temperatures show one decimal with a trailing .0 dropped, matching the web. Use the shared formatter for subtitles.
why: Number format on screen, decided by the shared pattern and web parity.

author: A
request: The app froze for a few seconds when I opened the Studio and the remote sheet was loading with Wi-Fi off.
plan: The Studio remote controller builds its app list synchronously on the main actor and waits on a service response with no timeout. Move the work off the main thread and treat no response as a dropped request, as the weather store does with its 20 s timeout. Add a test with a caller that never answers.
why: A hang fix; one sensible answer.

author: A
request: Opening a room doesn't always move it up in the Quick Links order.
plan: The increment script call is fired as the push begins and is dropped if the connection is momentarily not ready, so the access counter misses the visit. Queue the call until the connection is ready or retry once; the web has no retry. The ranking logic itself is unchanged.
why: A logic bug in counting visits; no screens change.

author: A
request: When I open the grill or fan sheet it covers everything. I want to see the room card behind it while I use it.
plan: Device sheets use the .hassSheet(.form) large detent and the modal-sheet pattern says form sheets are large, with the humidifier on page sizing. The owner's request would add a medium detent: options are medium with drag to large, medium only for the fan and grill, or a floating compact control.
why: Changes sheet detents; no decision on record for these sheets.

author: A
request: When the garage door command fails the tile says Error for ages and I can't tell if it's stuck.
plan: The Security spec and GarageDoorController show a red 'Error' for 8 s (web parity), while the optimistic-actions pattern says a rejected call shows its failed face for 4 s. Nothing says which the garage tile should follow. Options: keep 8 s, align to 4 s, or hold until the next tap; the face itself is the same.
why: Only how long an existing Error face stays; no decision on the value.

author: A
request: I tap the garage and the tile just says 'Sending Open…' and sits there. Can it show something that it's actually working and not hang there so long?
plan: The tile reads 'Sending Open…' until the call is acknowledged (at least 1 s), then reverts to the optimistic state; taps are ignored for 2 s. The action-tiles pattern only has a disc and text, with no progress treatment, and the web matches the current copy. Options: a progress ring on the disc with the same wording, or a shorter 'Sending' window and the optimistic Opening state straight away.
why: Changes the sending-state timing and what is drawn on the tile; no decision on record.

author: A
request: I'm standing right at home and the disarm confirmation pop-up every time is annoying. Can I just tap Disarmed?
plan: The native app asks 'Disarm the Security System?' as a recorded departure from the web (which disarms at once), citing HIG Alerts for a consequential action. Arming sends immediately. Options: keep the alert, drop it entirely, or ask only when the panel is armed Away or Night and disarm Home without asking.
why: Removes or conditions an alert; the recorded departure is what the owner is reopening.

author: A
request: The Front Door tile says Locked but my phone's lock app says it's unlocked.
plan: After a lock.unlock call fails the tile kept its optimistic 'Locked' value instead of rolling back to Home Assistant's state. The optimistic-actions pattern says a failed call rolls back exactly the values it committed and the state follows the live entity. Roll back in the lock controller's failure path and add a test.
why: A stale state corrected to the live value; existing pattern gives the answer.

author: A
request: The alarm card says 'Since 21:14' but my phone is on 12-hour time, it should say 9:14 PM.
plan: SecurityConfig.sinceText formats with a fixed 24-hour pattern. The schedule-date-fields pattern says times use the system locale format and the web shows locale time. Switch to the shared locale formatter, so 12-hour phones read 'Since 9:14 PM'.
why: Date format on screen, decided by the locale pattern.

author: A
request: Camera tiles are hard to read at night, the name label disappears into the picture.
plan: The tile shows only a small name label with a live dot over the picture; camera-streams and the Home notes keep it small because HIG HomeKit says not to cover camera views. Contrast of white on dark night frames is under 3:1. Options: a darker scrim behind the label, a small material pill, or move the name below the picture and shrink the picture.
why: Changes how a label is drawn over the video; several options.

author: A
request: After the phone's been asleep the cameras just show the still picture for a long time before the video starts.
plan: On resume the pool waits for the websocket to answer, restarts wanted streams, and tries WebRTC for 10 s before falling to HLS, which gets 25 s. Frames arrive sooner if the WebRTC wait is shortened, but a slow link would then fall to HLS needlessly and cost more data. Options: 10 s as is, 6 s, or probe WebRTC and HLS together.
why: Fallback wait times for the same stream modes; cost versus speed.

author: A
request: On the Security page the open doors list is in a random order, one time Garage is first and the next time it's last.
plan: The Contact Sensors sheet iterates a dictionary, so order is unstable; the Home overview lists rooms in config order and the room-overview-sheet pattern states config order for rooms. Use the same ordering for the Security chip sheet.
why: Order of items on screen, decided by the existing room-overview-sheet rule.

author: A
request: App crashed when I hit Disarm with no signal.
plan: SecurityScreen.canSend maps disconnected and rejected to 'cannot send', but the alert's confirm action force-unwrapped the connection that is nil while offline. Guard the call and surface the existing cannot-send path; add a unit test with a recording caller offline.
why: A crash fix with one correct answer.

author: A
request: The contact count flickers between 1 open and 0 open for a second when I close a door.
plan: The sensor goes closed then open then closed over about 800 ms while the latch settles, and each update repaints the chip and tile. No debounce exists; the web shows live values too. Options: no debounce, a 1 s settle on the count only, or 3 s for slower sensors; a longer settle delays a real open being shown.
why: Debounce of an existing count; same chip and tile.

author: C
request: After I hit Submit on a bug it sits on 'Filing your report on GitHub...' for ages and then jumps straight to the number. Can it feel quicker, and stay up long enough for me to read it?
plan: The form shows 'Uploading media n of m...' then 'Filing your report on GitHub...' as plain text and swaps to #N with View on GitHub; the integration answers synchronously, so the wait is the GitHub call itself. Options: a determinate bar for uploads with the done card held until tapped, or an auto-close after a few seconds. Nothing is recorded for either; the done card was ported from Festival's sheet.
why: Changes what is drawn and how long the done state stays (timing and drawn together), and no rule or recorded pick settles between the options.

author: C
request: I typed just the title in a Bug report and Submit is greyed out but nothing says why.
plan: The feedback spec says Submit is disabled with the reason shown (HIG Entering data; the settings-section pattern says to state why a control is disabled). `setTitle` keeps the '[Bug] ' prefix, so a title that is only the prefix passes the non-empty check but fails validation, and the `feedback.validation` line is skipped for that case. Show the existing validation line with the same wording style as the other reasons.
why: Restores a documented behaviour (disabled control states its reason) that a pattern already fixes; one answer.

author: C
request: The eight app icons in the picker are really hard to tell apart in that little list. Can I see them bigger?
plan: AppIconPickerSheet is a list of eight named rows with a small preview and a checkmark on the installed one. direction-g records the eight pairs and the default (Navy + Sky) but not how the picker is laid out. Options: a two-column grid of large previews with the name beneath, or keep the list and enlarge the preview to about 60 pt. No decision on record.
why: New layout of the picker with two plausible shapes and nothing on record to choose between them.

author: C
request: The number on the app icon goes stale for hours if I haven't opened the app. Can it keep up?
plan: Badge sync runs only while the app is open; closed, the icon keeps its last value and refreshes only when Fenton Push puts `aps.badge` on an alert push. Options: a BGAppRefreshTask (iOS runs it rarely and it needs a headless connection), more server pushes (silent pushes are throttled to about three an hour), or leave it. The badge, its number and the switch stay as they are in every option.
why: Only how often an existing badge refreshes, a battery and server-load trade-off with no change to anything drawn.

author: C
request: Reset to Default on the Background Blur slider leaves the wallpaper almost sharp, not in the middle where it started.
plan: The Appearance row documents a 0 to 100% slider in steps of 5 with a default of 50%, which is the web's 16.8 pt blur (page-backdrop R8, R9). Reset writes the step index (10 steps from the middle, stored as 5) instead of the percentage, so it lands near 5%. Store 50 as the documented default.
why: A wrong value corrected back to the default the page-backdrop record already states; the slider looks the same.

author: C
request: About says Version 0.1.0 (1) on my TestFlight build. Shouldn't it be the date one?
plan: Versioning is YYMM.DD.NN, stamped on release builds by `versioning.py build-settings`; local builds stay 0.1.0 (1). The TestFlight upload script ran without the stamping step, so the About row and the build text the Version row copies read the unstamped value. Run the stamp in the release path; the row's format is untouched.
why: A wrong value corrected to what versioning already defines, with no change of format or copy.

author: C
request: I signed out on bad wifi and the 'Signing Out' spinner just never stopped.
plan: Confirmed Sign Out asks the server to unlink the phone (`AppSession.confirmedSignOut`) and waits with no limit. The connection-lifecycle rule says a command something waits on takes a timeout (10 s, like the camera stream commands). On expiry the existing `signOutFailed` alert shows, and the owner already settled that there is no local-only sign out (2026-10-24).
why: Adds a missing timeout in front of an existing alert; recorded rules give the limit and the outcome, so one answer.

author: C
request: The notification permission and Time Sensitive stuff only shows up in that first-run setup. If I turn something off I can't find where to put it back.
plan: The Setup flow asks Notifications, Time Sensitive and Location in one sheet after sign-in; Settings has no row for them, and Appearance holds only 'Show count on app icon'. Today the only way back is the iOS Settings app. Options: a Notifications section showing the system state with a link to iOS Settings, or in-app switches for Time Sensitive too. No decision on record.
why: A new section or control in Settings with two possible shapes and nothing recorded.

author: C
request: My screen recordings get squashed to fit and look awful in the issue. Let me trim the clip before it goes.
plan: `FeedbackMediaFitter` shrinks each file to GitHub's 10 MB limit (JPEG steps, then export presets) and the attachment tile shows the result; there is no trim step. Options: open the system video editor from the tile, or show the fitted size and let the owner pick a quality before sending. Neither is recorded.
why: A new control in the attachment strip with no recorded rule choosing the approach.

author: C
request: I picked a new app icon and the row in Settings still shows the old one until I leave and come back.
plan: `AppIconSettingsRow` is documented to show the installed icon's preview and name. It reads the installed name once at render and does not refresh after `setAlternateIconName` completes, so the preview and name are stale until the screen rebuilds. Re-read `alternateIconName` after the call.
why: A stale state corrected to what the spec already shows; no new look.

author: C
request: At the biggest text size 'Request a Feature' and the Account rows get cut off.
plan: Settings rows are meant to wrap (the settings-section pattern; `SettingsScreen` is audited at AX5 and 44 pt targets). The Feedback row's label is fixed to one line. Let it wrap and keep the 44 pt minimum; HIG Typography (Dynamic Type) leaves one answer.
why: Visible layout fix decided by the existing pattern and HIG; no pick needed.

author: C
request: Five tabs is more than I use. Chores I'm in daily and Thermostat never. Let me reorder or hide tabs.
plan: The shell has a fixed tab list with Settings last (owner, 2026-10-16), and the iPad flyout lists the same five. Nothing on record about customising them. Options: the system's customisable tab bar (reorder and hide through the edit mode), or a list of tab switches inside Settings.
why: Changes which tabs a person sees and how they navigate; no decision on record.

author: C
request: Unfolded Duo held upright, the page title is tiny and tucked in the side bar. Looks off.
plan: Owner, 2026-10-30: unfolded portrait uses the normal iPhone title; unfolded landscape and partial landscape use 24 pt (header-edge-fade R7 (6)). The vertical-bar test (`shellInVerticalBar`) is true in unfolded portrait too, so the small title is applied there. Fix the test for that pose.
why: Brings a visible title back to a style the owner stated word for word; one answer.

author: C
request: On the iPad in landscape the flyout covers the page every time. Could it just stay open down the side?
plan: iPad uses an overlay glass flyout with the Open Navigation button top-leading (direction-g); iPad landscape may split, and the Duo uses the system's vertical bar. A pinned sidebar is not on record. Options: a persistent sidebar in landscape that collapses to the overlay in portrait, or keep the overlay but let it stay open until dismissed.
why: New navigation chrome for iPad landscape with no decision on record.

author: C
request: Scrolling feels janky again, especially after I've gone in and out of the app a bunch of times.
plan: Matches the resume-lifecycle findings: anything a resume registers and a background doesn't remove becomes steady cost (the paging scroll behaviour's records, AVPlayer observers). Read the `ResourceCensus` gauges after six cycles, find the registration that grows, and add it to `ResumeLifecycleTests`. Nothing on screen changes.
why: Scroll smoothness and memory only; the cause and test are covered by an existing pattern.

author: C
request: I opened the app this afternoon and it was on some Chores sub-page from this morning. Annoying. Other times I'm glad it remembered.
plan: A cold launch within 30 minutes of last use puts back each section's pushed pages (`RouteRestore.isFresh`, 2026-10-24); after that it opens at the roots. The screens are the same either way. Options: shorten the window to about 10 minutes, keep 30, or restore only the selected tab.
why: Only the window during which an existing restore applies; same screens, a convenience against surprise trade-off.

author: C
request: When I fold the Duo the open recipe just jumps from the side pane to full screen. Make it glide, and hold a beat so it doesn't flicker while I'm still folding.
plan: Fold, unfold and rotation move an open detail between the trailing pane and a push one run-loop turn after the window update, unanimated (split-view). The mockups play the split opening and closing with `MotionTokens.standard`, but that covers opening and closing, not this hand-off. Options: standard motion after a short settle delay of about 0.3 s, or a 0.2 s cross-fade; neither is recorded for this move.
why: Adds motion where the rule says none and changes when it happens; no decision on record.

author: C
request: The Weather sheet has a text Done in the corner instead of the X like the others.
plan: The modal-sheet pattern (owner, 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-24) puts the circle-X `SheetCloseItem` in `.primaryAction` on every sheet built on `HassModal`, and never a text Done. The weather sheet builds its own toolbar. Move it onto `HassModal`, which also gives its pushed pages Close beside Back.
why: Visible fix to an already recorded sheet convention.

author: C
request: Opening Vacuum from Settings there's a spinner for a second even though everything's already there. Feels slow.
plan: `ContentGate` on a cold page load holds the spinner at least 1 s and fades it out over 500 ms because the owner asked for the web's sequence (2026-10-16), against HIG Loading's show-content-at-once. The spinner, fade and page are unchanged by any option: keep 1 s, cut the minimum to about 0.4 s, or skip the hold when the data was cached.
why: Only how long an existing spinner is held; same look and motion, a feel against HIG trade-off.

author: C
request: On a Settings topic page, swiping from the left edge pulls out the menu instead of going back.
plan: Settings pushes are values on the tab's path, so `ShellNavigator.isAtRoot(.settings)` is false and the flyout leaves the edge swipe to the system back (2026-10-16). Vacation is pushed with a plain NavigationLink, which isn't in the path, so `isAtRoot` stays true there. Register Vacation as a `SettingsRoute` value like the other topics.
why: Fixes navigation to the behaviour already recorded for Settings pushes.

author: C
request: On the iPad in landscape, tapping a room covers everything with a sheet. It'd be nice if rooms opened next to the list.
plan: The on-demand split pattern exists (full width first, the item opens in the trailing half, Back closes it first; iPad landscape only, never in portrait), and its notes name rooms as a next candidate. Rooms today open as page-size sheets. Options: a trailing room pane on iPad landscape with sheets kept elsewhere, or keep sheets and widen them. No decision on record.
why: Changes how a tap opens a room on iPad; the pattern allows it but nothing says rooms should move.

author: C
request: Unfolded Duo, landscape, the app locks up for a few seconds and the whole page looks frozen.
plan: Matches the hinge rule: a view that measures its frame inside hinge-dependent padding flips its inset every layout pass and pins the main thread (found with `ChipRail`). Measure the full-width frame outside that padding and add the unfolded-simulator journey. No layout change.
why: A hang fixed by an existing measuring rule; nothing drawn differently.

author: A
request: Water now starts at 10 minutes, can you make that the default? 15 is too long for the faucet zones.
plan: The Water now run time starts at 15 minutes (web default, range 1 to 60 with a stepper). The owner has named the value, 10, so it only changes the stepper's starting number for all zones; nothing is drawn differently and the web would keep 15.
why: A stated default value; the owner already chose it.

author: A
request: The default run time in Water now is too long. Pick something saner.
plan: The stepper starts at 15 min, the web's default, and Garden Faucet zones water a small bed. No per-zone default exists and no decision is recorded. Options: 5 min for all, 10 min for all, or remember the last run time per zone; the last choice needs storage.
why: Starting value of an existing control; owner must pick the value or rule.

author: A
request: Sidewalk zone still says Watering about a minute after it stopped.
plan: buildSprinklerSnapshot reads a valve as watering when its state is open or opening, and the native card also treated the last hourly history entry as still running for its run_time window. The snapshot port should follow sprinklerState.ts rule for rule, which uses only the valve state. Remove the history-based fallback and add a test with a closed valve.
why: A stale state corrected to the documented rule.

author: A
request: The battery warning should show up earlier than 20%, I don't want to find it dead.
plan: The low battery alert shows at 20% or less, ported from the web. Options: 30% (earlier warning, appears more often), 25%, or per-controller thresholds; the alert text 'Battery N%' and its position above the card stay the same.
why: Threshold for when an existing alert appears.

author: A
request: When I hit Start watering it just sits there for ages before anything happens. Show me it's working, and don't make me wait for the 10 seconds.
plan: The write shows optimistically and reverts after 10 s if nothing confirms; the pushed page keeps the button pinned and returns on success. There is no in-progress state on the button and the web has none. Options: a spinner inside the pinned button with the same label, a shorter 5 s revert with an inline message, or return to the controller sheet at once and show Starting on the zone row.
why: Changes the wait and what the button draws; no decision on record.

author: A
request: The Stop watering label is really pale in light mode, I can barely read it.
plan: The notes record that system red is 3.6:1 on a light grouped row, and 'Stop watering' is meant to use HassTokens.Ink.danger. The newly added Controls section renders it with the default role tint instead. Use Ink.danger as documented and add the AX contrast check.
why: Colour restored to the recorded token.

author: A
request: Next watering on the card says 7:00 AM but the schedule says 6:30.
plan: Schedule rows show start_times as time of day and the card takes the earliest of the active programs. The native card parsed a UTC timestamp from the history attributes as local time, so it offset by the zone. The spec says times show as time of day only, from the program's own start_times; read those instead.
why: A time value corrected to the spec's source.

author: A
request: Can Rain delay be 12, 24 or 48 hours instead of fixed 24?
plan: The spec has a Rain delay toggle labelled 'Rain delay · 24 hours' that sends switch.turn_on or turn_off; the B-hyve integration exposes only that switch for it. A picker would need a service or helper to carry the duration. Options: a segmented 12/24/48 choice, a menu on the row, or leave the switch and rename the label.
why: New control and copy; no decision on record.

author: A
request: When my schedule Apply fails the red message stays on the page forever.
plan: Failures show Home Assistant's message inline and it stays until the next write; the optimistic-actions pattern clears failed state after 4 s on tiles. Options: clear after 8 s, after 4 s as on tiles, or stay until edited; the same message, in the same spot.
why: How long an existing inline error stays.

author: B
request: When I spin the vacation end date wheel it saves the first date I land on, then saves again, and the page flickers.
plan: Inline Vacation Dates commit after 0.9 s without a change so turning a wheel sends one call. A slow spin pauses more than 0.9 s, so it sends two. Options: raise the pause to 1.5 s (slower to apply), or send only on losing focus. The wheels and sheets stay identical.
why: Only a debounce interval changes; the same picker and page.

author: B
request: Every time I open Vacation after the app was in the background it says Setup required for a second.
plan: The Setup required alert waits 5 s of unavailable command state, but at launch it shows at once; a resume from background counts as a launch since the sensor is unavailable until reconnect. Options: apply the 5 s wait after a resume too, or 2 s. Alert text and place unchanged.
why: Threshold deciding when an existing alert shows.

author: B
request: Ending a Solo Trip should ask me first like turning off Vacation Mode does.
plan: Turning an engaged Vacation Mode off asks 'Turn Off Vacation Mode?' with a plain Turn Off (owner, 2026-10-13); alert-conventions say only data loss is destructive. End Solo Trip applies at once with a 60 s optimistic revert. No decision on record for the trip. Options: an alert 'End Solo Trip?', or an Undo bar.
why: Adds a confirmation or navigation step with no decision on record.

author: B
request: The Solo Trip sheet shows the return time in 24-hour but the page below says 3:00 PM.
plan: The date-field pattern formats every picker and summary with the device's time style. The sheet builds its own 24-hour formatter instead of using ScheduleDateFields' shared one. Switch it to the shared formatter; the picker and copy stay the same.
why: Format of a displayed time corrected to the shared pattern.

author: B
request: After I confirm vacation dates the page shows 'end must be after start' for a second then goes away.
plan: Confirmed dates stay on screen until both input_datetime helpers echo, with a 10 s fallback. The hold ends when the first helper echoes, so the new start meets the old end for a moment. Release the hold only after both echo. The error text itself is unchanged.
why: A transient wrong state corrected; the screen and copy remain as designed.

author: B
request: Sometimes Confirm Vacation says it couldn't apply, but a minute later the vacation is on.
plan: Household away commands time out after 10 s and report an unknown outcome; the script sometimes echoes later than that. Options: raise the timeout to 20 s, or keep 10 s and show the unknown outcome as 'checking' until the sensor settles. The first leaves the message as it is.
why: blind: one option changes the copy to 'checking'

author: B
request: The traveler buttons in Solo Trip are just names. Can they show the person's picture?
plan: Travelers are GlassTiles with names. The avatar pattern covers every tile that stands for a person (Profile, resident pages), with initials fallback, so the tile adopts the Avatar component the way other people tiles do. The selected trait and sizes are unchanged.
why: Adopts an existing pattern component; decided by the avatar pattern.

author: B
request: When I set up a Solo Trip the return time starts at the current time, so I always have to change it.
plan: The native sheet starts Returns at now; the web's defaultReturn is the next 9:00 am (ha-sfenton-react-dash SoloTripPage). The control is the same date-and-time picker. Match the web's starting value.
why: A default value of an existing field set to what the web already does.

author: B
request: On the vacation checklist I'd like to see how many items are done, like 3 of 5.
plan: The checklist is a ModuleList of toggle rows with Checked / Not checked values; the page shows no progress. The web shows none. Options: a count in the section header, or a progress ring in the Vacation Mode tile.
why: Adds an element with no decision on record.

author: B
request: The map takes forever to show the robot when I open the sheet.
plan: The map poll runs every 3.5 s and the first request waits for the next tick, so the robot position arrives up to 3.5 s after the PNG. Options: poll at once on open then every 3.5 s, or every 2 s while cleaning, which costs battery and more traffic. The map and robot icon look the same.
why: Only when the existing robot marker appears changes; trade-off of polling cost against latency.

author: B
request: The map keeps refreshing and flickering every few seconds even when the vacuum is just sitting in the dock.
plan: The map polls every 3.5 s whenever the robot is considered live, which includes docked. Pausing to 30 s while docked and idle, with an immediate poll on a status change, would cut data and CPU; the cost is a slower first update when the robot starts. The map draws the same.
why: Polling interval for an unchanged screen; a data and battery trade-off.

author: B
request: The sheet title says Docked 98% but the Battery tile says 100%.
plan: The subtitle reads the vacuum's battery_level attribute and the Battery tile reads the separate battery sensor, which lags. The pattern says the tiles mirror the subtitle. Read both from the vacuum entity.
why: A wrong value corrected to the one the sheet already shows.

author: B
request: The cleaning report still has room names on the map. I thought we took those off.
plan: Owner 2026-10-28 removed room names from the map; the area editor and the report use the same map without names. The report builds its own scene with drawNames left on from before. Remove it there; rooms are named elsewhere.
why: Drawn text removed to match a recorded owner decision.

author: B
request: When I change Mode to Vacuum the Water row pops out and the card behind it jumps instead of closing smoothly.
plan: The pattern specifies the row reveal through VacuumRevealLayout: height animates with the standard 0.3 s curve and the card's corners follow. The Mode picker path bypasses the animation transaction when the new value is applied from the menu. Route it through the same withAnimation call; Reduce Motion cross-fades.
why: Motion brought back to what the pattern already specifies.

author: B
request: Could the bin level show in the status tiles under the map?
plan: Status, Battery and Dock are three equal read-only tiles in one row; values never size a tile and it becomes one column at accessibility sizes. A fourth tile would break the three-up row. Options: a 2 by 2 grid, replace Dock's tile when docked, or put bin level in the Info section.
why: Adds an element and changes a layout rule with no decision on the layout.

author: B
request: The Clean button just says Clean. When I've picked three rooms it should say so.
plan: One blue Clean PrimaryButton, labelled Clean in both Rooms and Area modes (vacuum-sheet redesign, 2026-10-28); the summary row above lists the order chips. The decision was about the two modes, not the count. Options: 'Clean 3 Rooms', 'Clean Selected Rooms', or keep the label and add the count to the footer.
why: Changes copy where the recorded label does not cover the new case.

author: B
request: Starting a clean from the app sometimes says the robot didn't start when it actually is just waking up.
plan: A queued clean fails if the robot isn't cleaning within 30 s of the script call. A robot that has to leave a drying dock can take 40 s. Options: 60 s, 45 s, or 30 s only when docked idle. The failure message and the sheet are the same either way.
why: Only a timeout for an existing error changes.

author: B
request: The Main Floor Auto-Clean switch goes back off after a few seconds even though the robot accepted it.
plan: The Main Floor pause switch is inverted (on means not paused). Confirmation compares the echoed state without inverting, so the 8 s revert fires on a correct echo. Compare through the same inversion as the display. The row's look is not touched.
why: Logic bug where a correct state is reverted; one right answer.
